title: MySQL Quiz
description: Fourteen questions covering the whole MySQL tutorial: server and client, databases and types, CRUD, filtering, joins, aggregates, indexes, users, transactions, backups and dialect differences.

questions.question: Which storage engine is the default in MySQL 8.4 and provides transactions, row locks and foreign keys?
questions.explanation: InnoDB has been the default engine since 5.5. MyISAM is the legacy engine without transactions or foreign keys; MEMORY and CSV are special-purpose engines.

questions.question: In the mysql client, `-P` (capital) sets the port and `-p` (lower case) asks for the password.
questions.explanation: The two options differ only in case: -P 3306 is the port, -p prompts for the password. The default port is 3306.

questions.question: In MySQL, `utf8` is an alias for the four-byte `utf8mb4` character set.
questions.explanation: utf8 is an alias for utf8mb3, the old three-byte encoding that rejects emoji and many other characters. Always write utf8mb4 explicitly.

questions.question: Ending a statement with `___` instead of a semicolon makes the mysql client print each row vertically, which is how you read `SHOW CREATE TABLE` output.
questions.explanation: \G prints every column on its own line, labelled. It is a client command, so it works for any query.

questions.question: Which type converts values to UTC when storing them and back to the session time zone when reading them?
questions.explanation: TIMESTAMP is stored as UTC and converted on the way in and out; DATETIME is stored exactly as written with no time zone handling. DATE and TIME have no zone either.

questions.question: This UPDATE is executed twice in a row. What does the client print the second time?
questions.explanation: The WHERE clause still matches the one row, but its stock is already 30, so nothing changes. Rows matched counts matches, Changed counts actual modifications.
questions.code: UPDATE coffees SET stock = 30 WHERE id = 3;

questions.question: The MySQL-specific null-safe equality operator, which returns 1 when both sides are NULL, is written `___`.
questions.explanation: <=> compares like = but treats two NULLs as equal and NULL versus a value as not equal, returning 0 or 1 instead of NULL.

questions.question: With 7 orders and 5 customers, how many rows does `SELECT * FROM orders JOIN customers;` return?
questions.explanation: Without an ON clause MySQL performs a cross join, pairing every order with every customer: 7 × 5 = 35 rows. There is no error message.

questions.question: With the default sql_mode this query fails with error 1055. Why?
questions.explanation: ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY requires every selected column to be grouped or aggregated. ordered_at is neither, so MySQL refuses to pick an arbitrary value. Use MAX(ordered_at), add it to GROUP BY, or wrap it in ANY_VALUE().
options: ordered_at is neither grouped nor aggregated, which ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY forbids
GROUP BY requires an ORDER BY
customer_id must come last in the SELECT list

questions.question: An index on `(origin, roast)` can be used to satisfy `WHERE roast = 'dark'` on its own.
questions.explanation: A composite index is sorted by its first column; a condition on the second column alone cannot use it (the leftmost-prefix rule). It serves origin alone or origin plus roast.

questions.question: Which authentication plugin is the default in MySQL 8.4 and the only built-in password plugin remaining in 9.0?
questions.explanation: caching_sha2_password has been the default since 8.0. mysql_native_password was deprecated, disabled by default in 8.4 and removed in 9.0; auth_socket is used only for local root on some Linux packages.

questions.question: InnoDB's default transaction isolation level is ___.
questions.explanation: REPEATABLE READ gives each transaction a consistent snapshot from its first read. PostgreSQL defaults to READ COMMITTED instead.

questions.question: Which backup tool was deprecated in 8.0.34 and removed in MySQL 8.4?
questions.explanation: mysqlpump is gone; mysqldump remains and MySQL Shell's util.dumpInstance and util.loadDump are the recommended parallel tools.

questions.question: Under MySQL's default collation `'Mei' = 'mei'` is true, while in PostgreSQL the same comparison is false.
questions.explanation: utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci compares case-insensitively; PostgreSQL compares exactly unless you use ILIKE or a case-insensitive collation.
